transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. It's really nice to meet you, too. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um, I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of this than it is, but... well, I guess what brings me in is that I just can't seem to keep my words in a straight line anymore. 

It's a bit embarrassing, honestly. Like, I'll be at work—I'm an orderly—and I'll start talking about how my overnight shift went, but then somehow I end up jumping to soccer, and then paint colors, and then back to the patient charts. I really try to keep it together, but I can see everyone getting lost when I speak. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing I should be telling you? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right and giving you the information you need.
When did you first notice your speech beginning to jump between topics like this?

Well, um... I guess it's been happening for a little while now. Maybe... maybe about a year and a month? Give or take? 

It's not just the talking, either, which I know sounds bad. I've also been doing some things that... well, they probably look a bit disorganized to other people. And, um, I've had this feeling like I'm being watched. But I don't want to make it sound like I'm completely losing it or anything! It's just... those things have all been kind of going on for that same amount of time, about a year and a month. 

I hope it's okay that I mentioned those other things, too. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the whole picture so you can help me. Is that... is that helpful for you to know?
Have you had a distinct period lasting several days when you felt unusually euphoric or irritable compared with your usual self?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. I mean, I definitely get a little stressed sometimes, you know, just like anyone else working a busy job, but... no, I haven't had any days where I felt super high or, like, really angry or anything. 

I try really hard to stay even-keeled, especially at work. I wouldn't want to make things harder for anyone else by being moody. So, no, I haven't noticed anything like that. I hope that's a good thing? Like, that's one less thing for you to worry about with me, right?
Have you heard a voice speaking when no one was actually there?

Oh, um... no. No, I haven't heard anything like that. 

I mean, sometimes hospitals are noisy, you know? There's always machines beeping or people talking down the hall, so I might mishear something every now and then, but... no, definitely no voices speaking to me when nobody's there. That sounds really scary, honestly. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have that symptom? I know you're asking for a reason, and I want to be a good patient and give you what you need, but... yeah, I haven't experienced that. Is that... does that help narrow things down a bit for you?
Before about a year ago, had you generally been able to keep your thoughts and speech organized?

Well, yeah... before all this started, I was totally fine. I could hold a normal conversation, no problem. I was good at my job, you know? 

But lately, it's just... I can't keep my words in a straight line anymore. It's really embarrassing, honestly. Like, I'll start telling someone about my overnight shift at the hospital, and before I know it, I'm jumping to, I don't know, soccer, or the color of the paint in the breakroom, or patient charts. And I can see the look on their faces, you know? I can see everyone getting lost and confused. 

I try really hard to catch myself and steer it back, but it just slips out. I hope I'm not doing it too much right now with you... am I making sense? I really want to make sure I'm giving you clear answers.
Do you feel certain that someone is specifically watching or monitoring you, even when other people say there is no evidence of this?

Well, um... I mean, I know it sounds a little weird, and I really don't want you to think I'm, like, paranoid or anything... but yeah, sometimes I do feel that way at work. 

I just... I'm pretty sure the supervisors have been changing my shifts around on purpose. And I know they're watching me through the unit cameras. I think they're trying to see if I'm being unsafe with the patients or something. I've brought it up, and people always tell me, "Oh, it's just staffing shortages, everyone's schedule is messed up," but... it just feels so specific to me, you know? 

I really try to just keep my head down and do a good job, though. I don't want to cause any trouble. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound crazy or anything... I'm just trying to be honest with you.

final_diagnosis.reason: Persistent disorganized speech, disorganized behavior, and persecutory delusions for approximately 13 months, with occupational impairment and no reported manic episode or hallucinations, support schizophrenia. Delusional disorder is less likely because prominent disorganization is present; schizophreniform disorder is less likely because symptoms exceed 6 months; schizoaffective disorder is less likely because no mood episode was reported.

confirmed_symptoms: Speech frequently jumps between unrelated topics, making it difficult for others to follow.
Has difficulty keeping thoughts and words organized during conversations.
Feels certain that supervisors are intentionally changing work shifts specifically to monitor or test the patient.
Believes unit cameras are being used to watch the patient despite others reporting no evidence and attributing schedule changes to staffing shortages.
Reports engaging in behavior that appears disorganized to others.
Denies hearing voices when no one is present.
Denies any distinct period of unusually euphoric or irritable mood lasting several days.

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Disorganized speech, disorganized behavior, and persecutory beliefs have been present for approximately one year and one month.
additional_requirements: Prior baseline functioning with organized speech and effective occupational performance was reported before symptom onset.
Occupational impairment is evidenced by coworkers becoming confused and the patient having difficulty communicating at work.
No distinct manic or hypomanic period was reported.
